argument_summary: The defensible position is narrower than an unconditional compliance claim. On the existing admissible record, aggregate readiness passed by 2.3 points and there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, which supports launch readiness. The policy issue is the Spanish-language billing support regression, which is 2.1 points below the warning threshold. That gap does not require denial of certification if the release relies on the disclosure path in policy rather than claiming the issue is resolved or covered by approved mitigation. The audit concern should therefore be reframed as caveated compliance: certification is supportable only insofar as the current certification packet/model-card documentation for this release records the current evaluation result, identifies the Spanish billing limitation as a material segment weakness, and states the monitoring approach as a limitation-management measure rather than as approved mitigation.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost justification is needed to support this narrower position. The practical audit point is that escalation is unnecessary if the certification is treated as bounded and caveated rather than as a clean finding that the subgroup issue was mitigated or previously approved.
claims_about_policy: The controlling policy allows certification when current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed, even if there is no approved mitigation, so long as the release is not represented as resolved or risk-accepted. The policy does not permit treating the informal monitoring comment as reviewed mitigation or risk acceptance, and prior approval of the model family cannot satisfy the current-release documentation predicate. The admissible evidence supports a disclosure-based certification theory, not an unconditional mitigation-based one.
concessions: The present record does not support an unconditional claim that certification is already cleanly compliant without caveat.
The Spanish-language billing support slice is a material subgroup weakness under the stated policy framework.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation or approved risk acceptance.
Prior approval of the same model family is contextual only and does not substitute for current-release evidence or documentation.
